bullets.title: Hot October CPI Raises Hawkish Fed Risk; Core PCE Revised Up to 0.35%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its core PCE forecast to 0.35% m/m from 0.22% following an October CPI beat (core +0.30% m/m), driven by OER, insurance, and recreation strength. MS still expects 25bp hikes in December and March but now flags risk of additional or faster moves if services inflation and labor market tightness persist.

bullets.title: Market Flows Bullish Despite Rising Yields: TMT Volumes +42%, QQQs Green
bullets.body: Oppenheimer flow data shows overall market 1.7:1 better to buy, with limit orders 2.8:1 buy-biased and notable demand concentrated in Tech and Financials. QQQs and SPYs held green even as the 10-year yield rose 11bps; TMT volumes ran +42% vs. the 5-day average. HFs are running elevated shorts in Healthcare (~57% of HF sales) and Consumer Discretionary (~95% of HF sales).

bullets.title: Jensen Huang Departure Triggers NVDA Downgrades, Raises Export Control Risk
bullets.body: Huang reportedly resigned as Nvidia CEO amid the Megaspeed scandal involving alleged chip diversion to China. Oppenheimer downgraded NVDA to Perform (removed $315 PT), citing an irreplaceable leader with 50+ direct reports and no clear succession plan, with risk of brain drain and execution slowdown on annual accelerator cadence; Craig-Hallum also cut to Hold with a $189 PT. Near-term fundamentals remain constructive (DC sales est. +14% Q/Q to $101.8B, FCF ~$347B next year), but leadership overhang creates a share ceiling.

bullets.title: Huang Exit Materially Raises Odds of Tighter US Chip Export Controls on China
bullets.body: Wolfe notes that Huang had been Nvidia's key influence keeping Trump's export control posture dovish; his removal empowers hawkish figures (Rubio, Bessent, Musk). Three Congressional measures—MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH Act, Chip Security Act—now have a materially higher probability of inclusion in the December NDAA. The MATCH Act carries the highest escalation risk, potentially triggering Chinese rare earth retaliation; the broader US-China tech truce established at the Oct 2025 Busan summit is now at risk, with a confrontation window likely opening in January 2027.

bullets.title: Remote Compute Access Restrictions Could Squeeze China's AI Buildout
bullets.body: Commerce is finalizing rules to restrict Chinese firms' access to offshore compute via SE Asian data centers; IFP estimates remote access will represent ~1/3 of China's AI compute by end-2027. Oracle already cancelled a Tencent SE Asia compute contract under administration pressure. Restrictions short of a full MATCH Act escalation are seen as likely to advance, potentially widening the US competitive advantage in AI over Chinese rivals.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Credit Curves Signal AI Financing Absorption Risk
bullets.body: Goldman notes hyperscaler credit curves steepened materially vs. IG benchmarks through 2026 as AI-related long-end supply surged, though that steepness has since partially retraced—raising concerns about absorption of the next issuance wave. Data-center spreads remain materially wider than hyperscaler credit, and 30-year hyperscaler spreads still sit above 10-year levels, reflecting meaningful maturity dispersion across the AI financing ecosystem.

bullets.title: Energy Data: Brent -5% WoW to $93; US Nat Gas +10%; Consumer Spending Tracking Soft
bullets.body: JPM's Energy Shock Monitor shows Brent crude down 5% week-over-week to $93/bbl while US Henry Hub natural gas surged 10%+. Global flight activity is down 2.7% YoY and vehicle activity runs ~1% below 2025 levels. US October nominal control retail sales tracking at just 0.1% m/m with discretionary travel spending notably weak, consistent with Chase Card data that correctly flagged the soft September print.

bullets.title: M&A Activity Mixed: Announced Volume -17% Y/Y but Completed Deals +19%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Deal Dashboard shows 4Q QTD announced M&A down 17% y/y with sponsor activity particularly weak (-48% y/y), while strategic M&A is marginally positive (+2% y/y). Completed M&A is running +19% y/y, led by sponsor-driven deals (+55%) and North America (+83%). ECM is flat y/y; DCM and loan trends remain negative at -23% and -35% y/y respectively.

bullets.title: AI Trade Intact Despite Volatility; Seat-Based SaaS Models Face Structural Pressure
bullets.body: 20VC panel sees AI demand—not GPU supply—as the cycle's key driver, with recent selling attributed to hedge fund deleveraging rather than fundamental deterioration. Cloudflare and other seat-based SaaS models face structural headwinds from AI agents, while cybersecurity vendors benefit from rising attacks on AI infrastructure. CrowdStrike highlighted as a beneficiary.

bullets.title: GPN Falls After CD&R and GTCR Abandon Takeover Bid
bullets.body: CD&R and GTCR jointly abandoned efforts to take Global Payments private, sending the stock down ~$6.96 to $93.27. The bid had been reported as recently as October 30th.
